subject: Communication
title: Compassion Fatigue: When Empathy Runs Out
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Compassion Fatigue: When Empathy Runs Out.

hook.text: Nurses, therapists, and social workers listen to pain for a living. Eventually, many stop feeling anything at all.

buildup.text: Compassion fatigue: emotional and physical exhaustion from prolonged empathetic engagement with others' suffering.

discovery.text: Charles Figley found that the most empathetic caregivers are most vulnerable. Their greatest strength becomes their risk.

twist.text: The antidote isn't less empathy — it's 'compassion satisfaction' and self-care. Rest heals the healer.

climax.text: You can't pour from an empty cup. Protecting your emotional health isn't selfish — it's what makes continued caring possible.

punchline.text: To keep listening to others, you must also listen to yourself.

quiz.question: Who is most vulnerable to compassion fatigue?

details.summary: Compassion fatigue occurs when empathic listening becomes draining rather than connecting. Therapists, nurses, and caregivers are most vulnerable, but anyone who listens to others' suffering regularly can experience emotional exhaustion and reduced empathy over time.
details.whyItMatters: Helpers who burn out cannot help anyone. Understanding compassion fatigue is essential for sustaining empathic capacity over a career.
takeaways: Empathic listening can deplete emotional resources over time
Helping professionals are most at risk of compassion fatigue
Self-care and boundaries are essential for sustained empathy

faq.question: How is compassion fatigue different from burnout?
faq.answer: Burnout comes from workload and organizational stress. Compassion fatigue specifically comes from absorbing others' emotional pain. You can be energized by your work but still become compassion fatigued. It often has a more sudden onset than the gradual grind of burnout.

faq.question: What are the warning signs of compassion fatigue?
faq.answer: Emotional numbness toward people's problems, dreading interactions that require empathy, intrusive thoughts about others' suffering, and a sense that nothing you do makes a difference. Physical symptoms include sleep disturbance, irritability, and difficulty concentrating.
